subject: Dedicated capacity: committed-phasing, sprint discounts & close timeline
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Jay Patel <jay.patel@optima.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed sprint-based MAP + commitment phasing for dedicated capacity

Jay —

Thanks again for the demo last week. As discussed, I sketched a short mutual action plan that ties OptimaAI's evaluation milestones to committed capacity and tempo-based discounts. High level:

- Phase 1 (0-6 weeks): small dedicated GPU pool for canary + latency SLO validation (1–2 A100 equivalents).
- Phase 2 (6–12 weeks): scale to sustained throughput for the search/qa workload (4 A100 eq).
- Phase 3 (post-eval): full production pool (8–16 A100 eq) with a 12/24-month term option.

Each phase includes a checkpoint for pricing adjustments and a one-time ramp credit if you commit to a multi-quarter term at Phase 3. I attached the Redwood_MAP_Template_v2.pdf and a GPU_sizing_sheet.xlsx with suggested pool sizes and expected throughput.

Two quick clarifications I want to flag up front:
1) Burst policy — we allow short bursts above committed baseline for spiky traffic; bursts are billed at a premium rate but capped for the first 90 days of production.
2) Canary run — we recommend a 72-hour canary to validate perf and KV-cache hit rates before scaling.

If Optima likes the approach, we can convert this into an SOW + schedule and get procurement looped in. Proposed internal owner for the MAP is Rachel (cc'd) who will own pricing and timelines.

Next step: can you confirm whether a 72-hour canary is workable and if procurement prefers a milestone invoice cadence (monthly vs. quarterly)?

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Head of Solutions — Redwood Inference
T: +1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Redwood_MAP_Template_v2.pdf (application/pdf), GPU_sizing_sheet.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

From: Jay Patel <jay.patel@optima.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@optima.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Oct 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed sprint-based MAP + commitment phasing for dedicated capacity

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear breakdown. A few quick items from our side:

- Canary: 72 hours is fine. We'll want test vectors that replicate production traffic (we'll share a sampling of logs).
- Burst policy: procurement will want hard caps and an escalator formula (e.g., X% over baseline billed at Yx rate). Can you provide exact language we can drop into the SOW?
- Pricing cadence: we prefer quarterly invoicing but are open to monthly for the trial phase.

Amy (procurement) is on cc — Amy, are there any gating constraints on terms or internal approval timelines? Our CFO prefers to close before Nov 5 if possible because of budget cycles.

—Jay

Cc: Amy Chen <amy.chen@optima.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Oct 2026 10:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed sprint-based MAP + commitment phasing for dedicated capacity

Jay/Amy —

Thanks — quick answers below and I've pasted suggested SOW language for the burst clause. Rachel will follow up with a numeric pricing proposal by Friday.

1) Burst clause (suggested SOW paragraph):
"During the first 90 days following production cutover, Customer may exceed the committed baseline by up to 150% for a maximum of 4 hours per 24-hour period without an overage invoice. Any sustained usage beyond the 150% buffer will be billed at 2.5x the standard committed unit rate. After the initial 90-day period, burst allowances revert to a contract-defined monthly cap and are billed at 1.75x committed rates."

2) Canary artifacts: please send a 24-hour traffic sample and we will build a 72-hour canary job to run against the 1–2 A100 eq pool.

3) Invoice cadence: quarterly invoicing OK for Phase 3; for the trial phase we recommend monthly (easier to reconcile usage and credits).

I'll also propose a phased discount schedule tied to committed term and pool size:
- 12-month term at Phase 3: 8% discount on committed baseline unit rate
- 24-month term at Phase 3: 14% discount + one-time ramp credit equal to 2 weeks of committed baseline capacity

If that aligns, Rachel will send an initial pricing worksheet with specific per-unit numbers and an estimate of expected token costs for your search workload.

Thanks,
Marcus

Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>, Amy Chen <amy.chen@optima.ai>
Date: Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:09:00 -0700
Subject: OptimaAI pricing worksheet & phased commit options

Jay/Amy —

Attaching the Optima_Pricing_Proposal.xlsx with three sizing lanes and the corresponding committed unit economics. Highlights:

- Lane 1 (Pilot): 1–2 A100 eq — $0.045 per 1k tokens committed baseline; burst premium 2.5x.
- Lane 2 (Scale): 4 A100 eq baseline — $0.038 per 1k tokens; 12-month term discount 8%.
- Lane 3 (Prod): 8–16 A100 eq baseline — $0.031 per 1k tokens; 24-month term discount 14% + 2-week ramp credit.

We've modeled your search workload and estimate the monthly committed token consumption for Lane 2 at ~1.2B tokens (see tab "usage_estimates"). If Optima commits to Lane 2 with a 12-month term we can start with a 30% prepaid credit that will be applied against the first two invoices.

Next actions I propose:
- Jay: confirm Lane preference (Pilot vs Scale vs Prod).
- Amy: confirm procurement cadence and whether Optima requires any bespoke language around data residency or audit rights.
- Marcus/Grace: I'll schedule a 30-minute call early next week to walk through tabbed assumptions in the spreadsheet.

Thanks,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive — Redwood Inference

Attachments: Optima_Pricing_Proposal.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: OptimaAI pricing worksheet & phased commit options

Rachel/Marcus —

Thanks for the worksheet — Lane 2 (Scale, 4 A100 eq) aligns best with our near-term needs. Procurement items:

- We need the burst clause verbatim in the SOW (please add exactly as Marcus proposed).
- Quarterly invoicing post-trial is preferred; we'll accept monthly during the pilot.
- Please share a short SOW + SOW change log and we will route for legal review. Our target is to have a signed SOW by 2026-11-03 to hit internal budget windows.

For execution: please open a HubSpot deal note and a DocuSign envelope. I attached a link to our procurement portal and added a DocuSign placeholder (we'll complete signatories once we have SOW language).

Best,
Amy Chen
Procurement Manager — OptimaAI
